observed_value: Four issuer_name cells include section/industry/instrument/terms text instead of only the issuer.
anchor_value: The source schedule separates clean Company cells from Investment, date, rate, cost, and fair-value terms.

culprit_citations.quoted_text: Newark FP Co-Invest, L.P. (8)(10) | Partnership ( 8,555,356 units) | 11/8/2023 | 8,572 | 8,572 | 0.4 | %
AF Eagle Parent, L.P. (8)(10) | Partnership Units ( 337,024 units) | 11/27/2023 | 11,364 | 11,364 | 0.5 | %

findings.detail: ASP Unifrax continuation note rows were stored with debt section, industry, issuer, instrument, acquisition date, reference rate, and interest rate text in issuer_name instead of the clean issuer ASP Unifrax Holdings, Inc.
Newark FP Co-Invest was stored with equity section, industry, partnership terms, and acquisition date in issuer_name though the source Company cell is Newark FP Co-Invest, L.P.
AF Eagle Parent was stored with equity section, industry, partnership units, and acquisition date in issuer_name though the source Company cell is AF Eagle Parent, L.P.

rationale: This is a Class 1 issuer_name parse-leak defect. The flagged values concatenate schedule section and industry labels plus Investment, date, reference-rate, and interest-rate text into issuer_name. In the raw source, the relevant schedule rows keep the clean company names in the Company column or row context, while the note/partnership terms are separate Investment/terms columns. Therefore the C206 flag is a real localized extraction error, not a false alarm.
